Nothing asks first, and nothing says what follows: if the player isn't back within 60 seconds, the match counts as a loss. Practice already asks 'Leave this game?', and Concede asks too. Once this is built, Back during a live match asks: 'Leave the match? It goes on without you. Come back within 60 seconds or it counts as a loss.' Stay is the default. Once the game is over, Back leaves at once, as it does now. ## Why - The match screen's rail draws `` (`apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx:569`). A press calls `navigate(to)` at once (`apps/web/src/routes/nav.tsx:56-63`). - Leaving the route closes the socket (`apps/web/src/game/net.ts:864`, `live.close(1000, 'leaving the match')`), and the server starts the disconnect grace. §9.5 (`spec/09-architecture.md:64`): 'Disconnect grace (60 s) and concede end the match as a loss'. - The client already has the tool. `guardLeaving` (R1754000, `apps/web/src/net/navigate.ts:43`) holds every `navigate` and every `popstate` off a page until the page lets the player go. Only the creator uses it (`apps/web/src/routes/creator.tsx:43`). - R765 gives practice its 'Leave this game?' question and the menus a Rejoin banner. A live online match gets no question and no word of the 60 seconds. ## Proposal - While the view has no result (`view.result === null`), `match.tsx` registers `guardLeaving`. A held move opens a small dialog built like `ConfirmConcede` (`apps/web/src/game/ConfirmConcede.tsx`). - Its words: 'Leave the match? It goes on without you. Come back within {seconds} seconds or it counts as a loss.' `{seconds}` is `DISCONNECT_GRACE_SECONDS` from the generated server config. - Its answers: Stay, which is focused and is Escape's answer, and Leave, which makes the held move. - The guard is released once the view has a result, and on unmount. - The co-op table is left out. There a disconnect hands the seat to the AI rather than losing (§13.8), so it needs other words, and it can follow later. - A new ruling amends R765 for online matches. The strings get their zh-CN entries. ## Where it lands - `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, a new dialog under `apps/web/src/game/`, and the i18n catalog. - §9.5 (`spec/09-architecture.md`), with a ruling note and `spec/pending/.md`. - Tests in `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx`. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] In a live match, pressing Back shows the dialog and the path stays `/match/`. Stay closes it and sends nothing; Leave goes to the menu. - [ ] A browser Back (`popstate`) during a live match is held the same way. - [ ] Once the view has a result, Back leaves at once with no dialog. - [ ] The number in the words comes from `DISCONNECT_GRACE_SECONDS`, not a literal (CLAUDE.md rule 9). - [ ] The dialog opens with the focus on Stay, and Escape answers Stay. - [ ] The tests are named after the new ruling, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes. ## Size and risks Medium: about 150 lines plus tests. Only one page holds the guard at a time (`navigate.ts`), so the match screen must release it on unmount, or the next page inherits it. A navigation the app makes on its own, such as a forced one, must not be held. `navigate`'s `force` option covers that, and a test should show it. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it. Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it. ## Plan _Written by `claude-7` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41061030194)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal While `/match/` shows a live view (no result, and a socket that is neither voided nor refused), `guardLeaving` (R1754000) holds every way off the board: the rail's Back, the browser's Back and every unforced `navigate`. Leave makes the held move. Once the view has a result, Back leaves at once. The guard is released then and on unmount. Ruling R2479000 amends R765 and §9.5 cites it. The strings get zh-CN entries, and the tests in `match.test.tsx` carry the ruling's name. Come back within ${String(DISCONNECT_GRACE_SECONDS)} seconds or it counts as a loss.`;`` and `const AT = paths.match("m-1");` - `function Shell(): ReactElement`. Wrap this refused part in `vi.spyOn(console, "error").mockImplementation(() => undefined)` and restore it in `finally`, as the refused test at line ~1357 does. - Click Back: no dialog, path `paths.landing`. 6. **`it("R2479000 a forced move goes at once, an unforced one is held, and the guard leaves with the route")`** - `act(() => { navigate(paths.together); })`: the dialog shows, and the path is `AT`. Stay closes it and sends nothing; Leave goes to `/` (test 1). - [ ] A browser Back is held the same way (test 3). - [ ] Stay has the focus when the dialog opens, and Escape and Back answer Stay (tests 1, 2). - [ ] With a result, Back leaves at once and a question still open closes (test 4). - [ ] A voided or refused match is left at once (test 5). - [ ] A forced `navigate` is not held, and unmount releases the guard (test 6). - [ ] No literal 60 in code: the words read `DISCONNECT_GRACE_SECONDS` (rule 9). - [ ] The commands above and the harness's checks pass. - [ ] `git status` shows only the 8 files in the table. ## Risks - **A guard left behind.** Only one page holds the guard at a time, so the effect's cleanup must call `release()` (test 6). - **Hook order.** The new `useState` and `useEffect` must sit above `if (view === null)`, or React throws on the first view. - **The held browser Back.** Use `onLeave={leaving.leave}` exactly; test 3 fails if the dialog closes first. I checked this history sequence in a throwaway test against `ConfirmConcede`, along with the mock swap and the rail's Back on a finished match. All of it passed, and I deleted the test afterwards. - **Existing tests.** They keep the bare `vi.fn()` `navigate`. Only the new describe swaps in the real one, and it resets it after each test. Keep the describe last in the file, because it moves `window.location`. `match.test.tsx` passes on the base (64 tests). - **Rule 7.** The dialog reads nothing from the view and sends nothing. Leaving only unmounts the route, which closes the socket as it did before. - **i18n.** `i18n.test.ts` fails on a `t()` literal with no zh-CN entry, or on a `{seconds}` mismatch. Copy the keys byte for byte. - **e2e.** No spec leaves a live match by either Back: spec 19 uses `cy.visit("/")`, a full page load the guard never sees. If a spec does hit `leave-match-dialog`, report it; do not change e2e. ## Open questions None of these block the build. The issue left these decisions open; the ruling records each one: - **Voided or refused socket:** left at once. Otherwise the voided notice's "Back to the lobby" would ask about a match that no longer exists. - **Before the first view:** nothing is held. - **A result arriving while the question is open:** it closes the question instead of making the held move. - **Reload or closed tab:** no `beforeunload` prompt, since a reload rejoins the match. - **Leave button:** reuses the existing "Leave" string and Concede's red button. --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-10-30T13:03:04Z: Approve ````
